title: Generated Evidence Snapshots
purpose:
Define the generated evidence snapshot model used for point-in-time proof and
attestation reporting without turning that evidence into canonical requirement
text.
scope:
This specification covers evidence snapshot shape, well-known evidence kinds,
evidence statuses, partial collection semantics, overlap and merge behavior,
Source Context Notes as evidence-discovery inputs, and the rule that exact
discovery conventions remain tool-specific rather than canonical.
context:
Repositories often need machine-produced evidence from multiple tools. Unit
tests, benchmarks, static analyzers, code-mapping tools, manual evidence
imports, and human-authored Source Context Notes may all contribute to the same
requirement set. The standard therefore needs a shared output contract for
evidence without dictating how every language, framework, or build system
discovers it.

requirements.title: Keep evidence snapshots derived rather than canonical
requirements.statement:
Generated evidence snapshots MUST be treated as derived outputs rather than as
canonical requirement artifacts or a fifth canonical artifact family.
notes: Requirements remain the canonical statement of intent.
Evidence snapshots record point-in-time observations about repository truth.

requirements.title: Identify evidence snapshot provenance
requirements.statement:
An evidence snapshot MUST record a stable snapshot identifier, generation
timestamp, and producer identity.
notes: Producer identity usually includes a tool name and version.

Repositories may add commit hashes, branch names, workspace paths, or other
namespaced local metadata.

requirements.title: Record requirement-scoped observations
requirements.statement:
An evidence snapshot MUST record observations by `REQ-...` identifier and
evidence kind, with one status per observation entry.
notes:
Observation entries may also carry free-form refs, summaries, or namespaced
local metadata.

requirements.title: Keep evidence kinds extensible and machine-friendly
requirements.statement:
An evidence kind MUST use a lowercase token that starts with a letter and then
uses only lowercase letters, digits, or underscores.
notes: This keeps the kind easy to transport across tools and JSON outputs.

requirements.title: Define well-known evidence kinds without closing extension
requirements.statement:
The standard MUST define well-known evidence kinds while allowing repositories
and tools to emit additional kinds.
notes:
Well-known kinds include `unit_test`, `integration_test`, `manual_test`,
`benchmark`, `fuzz`, `security_scan`, `code_ref`, and `source_coverage`.
Custom kinds remain valid when they follow the canonical token pattern.

requirements.title: Keep evidence statuses canonical and finite
requirements.statement:
An evidence observation status MUST use one of `observed`, `passed`, `failed`,
`not_observed`, `not_collected`, or `unsupported`.
notes: `not_observed` means the tool checked and did not find matching evidence.
`not_collected` means the snapshot does not claim collection for that case.

`unsupported` means the producer cannot collect that evidence kind in the
current environment or stack.

requirements.title: Allow partial evidence collection
requirements.statement:
An evidence snapshot MAY cover only a subset of requirements or only a subset
of evidence kinds.
notes:
Partial collection is normal when different tools own different evidence
kinds.

requirements.title: Merge overlapping evidence snapshots additively
requirements.statement:
Derived reporting MUST treat multiple evidence snapshots as additive inputs
rather than require one combined master evidence file.
notes:
A repository may carry separate snapshots for unit tests, benchmarks, manual
QA, or other sources.

Equivalent observations may be deduplicated during reporting, but the
standard does not require one universal deduplication formula.

requirements.title: Avoid negative inference from snapshot absence
requirements.statement:
Reporting MUST NOT infer that evidence is absent from the repository solely
because one evidence snapshot omits a requirement or evidence kind.
notes: Omission from one snapshot means that snapshot made no claim.

Reporting may still conclude that evidence is absent when all relevant
snapshots for the evaluated scope explicitly support that conclusion.

requirements.title: Keep discovery conventions outside the core standard
requirements.statement:
The core standard MUST NOT prescribe one universal discovery convention for how
tools extract evidence from programming languages, frameworks, or repositories.
notes:
Tooling may use language-specific comments, attributes, manifests, naming
conventions, static analysis, metadata files, or other local mechanisms.
The core standard defines the output contract, not the extraction algorithm.

requirements.title: Treat Source Context Notes as optional authoring aids
requirements.statement:
A Source Context Note that uses `CONTEXT` and `SEE` markers MAY be used as a
non-canonical authoring aid to explain the durable context for nearby source.
notes: Source Context Notes are written for humans first.

They are useful when maintainers need to know why code is shaped a certain
way, where a value came from, what invariant must be preserved, or what
external artifact explains the decision.

requirements.title: Keep Source Context Notes non-canonical and non-proof
requirements.statement:
A Source Context Note MUST be treated as non-canonical; it is not verification
success.
notes:
If a note references a `REQ-...` identifier, that reference may support
evidence discovery, but generated evidence remains separate from the canonical
requirement record.

Source Context Notes do not replace requirement text, architecture rationale,
verification artifacts, or test results.

requirements.title: Document Source Context Note conventions
requirements.statement:
When a repository supports Source Context Notes, it MUST document the accepted
markers, reference categories, scoping rules, and local extensions.
notes:
Repositories may accept `CONTEXT`, `SEE`, and `END CONTEXT` as a
language-agnostic convention while still allowing language-specific comment
syntax around the markers.

Documenting the convention prevents source-context style from becoming an
implicit or tool-private dialect.

requirements.title: Bound region-scoped Source Context Notes explicitly
requirements.statement:
A region-scoped Source Context Note MUST provide an explicit end marker or
equivalent machine-readable range metadata when its scope extends beyond the
immediately following declaration or statement.
notes:
Implicit scopes such as "until the next blank line" are difficult to review
and difficult for tools to collect consistently.
Single-line notes and declaration-local notes do not need an end marker.

requirements.title: Emit Source Context Notes through generated outputs
requirements.statement:
Tooling that collects Source Context Notes for SpecTrace reporting MUST emit
generated evidence observations instead of writing collected source locations
back into canonical requirement records.
notes:
The usual evidence kinds for collected notes are `code_ref` and
`source_coverage`.

Tools may also render a derived source context index for lookup and review.
Observation refs or namespaced metadata may carry file paths, line ranges,
symbol names, local reference tokens, and short human-readable reasons.
